newsitem.title: COSTA RICA: Costa Rica suspends rice tender for second time.
newsitem.headline: Costa Rica suspends rice tender for second time.

text.p: Costa Rica postponed for a second time a rice tender for 26,500 tonnes of rough rice or 18,000 tonnes of dehusked rice because of high international prices, a spokesman for the national rice industry said Tuesday.

"On Monday, we took the formal decision to suspend the purchase (tender)," Victor Cordero, who works for the private company Granos Basicos de Centroamerica, which has been organising the tender and represents national rice interests, told Reuters.
The tender was published April 10 with offers open to April 16. Cordero said the tender was suspended until further notice.
Five U.S. firms and one Chilean firm put forward bids. All offered to sell Argentine rice to Costa Rica, Cordero said.
Cordero said the suspension came because prices offered were 16 to 17 percent over local prices which are fixed and controlled by the government and part of the country's basic basket of goods.
"We have had problems with the government because for us it is impossible to bring the rice at a set price and sell at at a lower price," he added.

Cordero added that Alvaro Cordero had decided to step down from the post of executive director of Granos Basicos from Wednesday. "He resigned on March 30, giving personal reasons," Cordero said, adding he had occupied the post since May 1993.
Costa Rica first suspended this rice tender at that time for 30,000 tonnes of rough rice on March 24 on grounds of high bid prices, with some 16 firms bidding.
